[b]Meeting Callan[/b]
[sub]Days after Gearhart's defeat, he must meet with his fellow Nationals Verbena and Callan as they sit before the Thurian National Assembly. [/sub]]

The Thurian Nationals meet at the largest citadel in the Basin, situated across the Rúdhava River in the capitol of Thurgot. Lately, the city of Niamh had been feeling exceptionally ripe, with garbage spilling over into the streets and alleyways. Despite the vibrant history and the hub that Niamh is, there was no other place in Thurgot where you could feel a sense of access as well as minor dread. 

The waste management depart for the city has gone on strike- again. Callan shuffles over another pile of uncollected trash while digging through his satchel as we make our way up the street towards the citadels front steps. He fails to miss the goopy mystery fluid leaking from the heaps of garbage and grumbles in accordance. This is the third pair of Elk-Leather Loafers ruined by some sh*tty trash department. What more could they want? We already give them five national holidays off a year. FIVE! His face twists painfully as he shoots piercing looks every which way before crossing the street. I make an effort to mirror his frustration, but this is just one thorn out of millions in his side. 

You know, the big F.O. has immaculate streets. Maybe we should convene there for our next meeting! This is my vain attempt at getting him to lighten up, but if laughing off one of my ideas isnt enough then I can tell what sort of day hes having. We both know the National Board hasnt ever met off the peninsula, no matter how kindly I ask or how many administrative buildings we construct. He glances at me with a strictness, and I decide that no matter how close we may be as our respective nationals, there still remains a tension between his government and mine. 

I look over at Callan and drink him in more deliberately this time, recognizing the three decades of National Board shenanigans written across his forehead. Im familiar with these lines, if only because I see them deepen daily into my own face. He isnt an easy person to work with, but hes a gangly behemoth of both bureaucracy and Thurian pride. There isnt much else to say about Callan. Ive never known him to have a lover; he has no children either. Hell, the man hasnt ever owned a pet now that I think about it. We met and this has always been what we are for one another: diplomats between a fractured region of the continent. The world beyond the Basin seemed indifferent to our activities, and aside from the occasional passing ship, most Thurians preferred isolation to involvement in foreign affairs.

This works in our favor, of course. Callan and I both agree that despite our own internal resources, staging any military intervention with the countries around the Basin would prove deadly for all Thurians, not just one nation over another. Gearhart believes we could take on any of them, but theres a reason our Pomp & Circumstance are purely performative. There hasnt been a militant force in Thuria for the last fifty years, at least not one that could prove viable in conflict. Most of our might is unified through optics, not true force. 

Did you secure the island? He makes an effort to stay on task even though we are both exhausted. Please tell me that drunken b*stard was upset. I wouldve paid good money to see him slosh about, shaking his fist into the fog. 

He wasnt happy, thats for sure. But it seems he has a calmer disposition. He only called me a c*nt once! I let the giddy feeling flow through me despite knowing it was wrong to do so. Watching Gearhart flap around on the shores of Kyarn made me feel so powerful. I was more than happy to finalize on the expedition on behalf of the board and knew it wouldnt be enough without rubbing it in the Vikrans face. 

Good. Maybe now he can stick to managing Balchikka without sinking the d*mn thing into the water. I still cant believe they rejected our Constitutional Summit. Is he mad? Surely not every Vikran is as insane as he? Callan had been whining over the denial for years now and had made it his sole purpose to ensure Gearhart would regret it. So far, Callan had failed to do so. Gearhart and every Vikran on his island were more than happy to play ball, so long as everyone agreed to be cool about a lot of things we werent happy being cool about. 

We round the corner and make our way up the steps to the front hall. The citadel, built over 350 years ago, was beginning to show its age. Most of the marble had begun wearing down  in high traffic halls, and decades of kindergarten handprints now dirtied the walls of the primary atrium. 

Oh, you glorious old dome, I mumble to myself and the ceiling. Shining in the faded brass of my forefathers, arching up into the highest reaches of Niamhs sky, the citadel had been home to Thurian politics for a long while. This was the exact spot of the First Assembly, setting the precedent for more than three centuries of Thurian political escapades. Standing in the very middle of the famous Citadel Mandala was the poor-excuse-of-a-swash-buckling-pirate Gearhart. He was more presentable today that he typically is, which is a lot considering the dress code of his home country is Dont Be Naked. 

You both owe me an apology. A new crate of vodka, and potentially another round of monetary assistance. You broke my boys hearts! Hes speaking coherently, but the smell of alcohol is rich and promising. I fear if I step any closer I may breathe in enough to wipe me out for the rest of the afternoon. 

Abel, get over yourself. You knew better than to claim land you had no right to. Its a miracle some other patrol didnt sink you when they had the chance. We had to dispatch 15 Staggs to seal off the region for Verbena to even approach the island, and thats BEFORE you swaggered on over with three kids and a rusted vessel. 
Callan wasnt typically so vocal with his disdain, but it was well warranted. Gearharts face turned a deep purple, but he said nothing in response. Turning on one heel, he stormed off into the depths of the Citadel. 

What a sourpuss. 

You arent helping at all, Verbena. You cant come whining to the Assembly any time you want to one up him. Hes a National, whether we like him or not. 

I feel my brows furrow in the heat of embarrassment. I just-

Save it. The Assembly has a lot to say today, to all of us. Were lucky they cant hang us anymore. His tone is stoic, but his face reads anxious. He straightens his bowtie and flattens his vest, holding the strap of his satchel as he walks ahead. His consternation is blinding, but I let my emotions get the best of me. 

I take a beat before hurling a final insult at the two of them as I follow suit.  

[/spoiler]
